brief.headline: Qualify a second source immediately — they're in the distress zone and lost ₹-22.50 Cr last year; protect supply before pushing price.

priceAsk.summary: Target the Bprex price of ₹1.62/NOS for the LDPE bottle (down from ₹1.69) — that alone saves us ₹3.37 L/yr.
priceAsk.target: ₹1.62/NOS on LDPE BOTTLE 5ML WHITE OPAQUE (the price we already pay Bprex Pharma Packaging India)
priceAsk.basis: We're paying them ₹1.69/NOS for the same bottle; Bprex gives us ₹1.62/NOS — a 4.3% gap. Plus they're 100% a reseller (no manufacturing), so their price carries a middleman margin. We should pay what the item costs at a maker's gate, not a trader's markup.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Hold at 30 days — do not give them longer payment; their cash is stuck for 335 days (vs 70 for similar firms) so any payment delay will worsen their fragility.

brief.financialLeverage: They are very fragile: they lost ₹-22.50 Cr in FY2023-24, their money-health score is 1/10, and they sit in the distress zone (Altman Z -0.18). They owe 220.44 times their own cash. But we're a big customer — our ₹81.39 L is 7.21% of their ₹11.29 Cr in sales — so losing us would hurt. That gives us bargaining power, but push too hard on price and they may fold or cut us off. The smarter play: lead with supply-security (dual-source now) and use our 7.21% share to get the Bprex price, not a deeper squeeze.

evidence.point: They keep far less profit than rivals
We are a big slice of their sales
Their cash is stuck much longer than similar firms
We're overpaying vs our cheapest supplier on this bottle

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter with pharma bottles & caps capability; health score B (65/100), revenue ₹2569.83 Cr — a solid, profitable second source to qualify now.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers and pharma packaging — strong and profitable, direct fit for bottles and closures.

alternates.name: Bprex Pharma Packaging India (P) Limited
alternates.why: Already our supplier for the same LDPE bottle at ₹1.62/NOS — expand volume here to reduce Berry dependence.

risks: They're in the distress zone and made a ₹-22.50 Cr loss — supply could vanish if they tip over; do not put more volume through them without a qualified backup in place.
They're 100% a trader (no manufacturing) — if their upstream maker cuts them off or reprices, our supply and price both become unstable.
Owe 220.44 times their own cash — any cash-flow shock (a big customer delay, a bank call) could freeze deliveries to us.
Asking for the Bprex price is fair, but going below it may trigger a supply cut-off given their fragility — tread carefully and keep Manjushree warm as Plan B.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the relationship, but we need to talk about two things: bringing your LDPE bottle price to ₹1.62 — the rate we already pay elsewhere — and lining up a second source so we're both protected if anything changes.
